IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Representatives McIntire, Santos, Conway, McDermott and Kenney

Bill.BriefDescription: Making the local government tax treatment of software businesses uniform.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to uniform local business license taxes on softwarebusinesses; adding a new section to chapter 35.21 RCW; creating a newsection; and providing an effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that certainty anduniformity of tax treatment of the software industry is important tothe industry and consumers. The intent of this act is to make the taxtreatment of software clear and certain for local governments,developers, programmers, and consumers.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 35.21 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Any city that imposes a license fee or tax for the privilege ofdoing business measured by rates against gross receipts shall imposethe tax upon persons engaged in the business of creating, producing, orselling or licensing software only in accordance with this section. (2) The following definitions apply. (a) "Canned software" means software that is created for sale tomore than one person. p. 1 HB 1747 (b) "Custom software" means software created for a single person. (c) "Customization of canned software" means any alteration,modification, or development of applications using or incorporatingcanned computer software for a specific person. "Customization ofcanned software" includes individualized configuration of software towork with other software and computer hardware, but does not includeroutine installation. Customization of canned software does not changethe underlying character or taxability of the original canned software. (d) "Master copies" of software means copies of software from whicha software developer, author, inventor, publisher, licensor,sublicensor, or distributor makes copies for sale or license. (e) "Retained rights" means any and all rights, includingintellectual property rights such as those rights arising fromcopyrights, patents, and trade secret laws, that are owned or are heldunder contract or license by a software developer, author, inventor,publisher, licensor, sublicensor, or distributor. (f) "Software" means any information, program, or routine, or anyset of one or more programs, routines, or collections of informationused, or intended for use, to convey information that causes one ormore computers or pieces of computerrelated peripheral equipment, orany combination thereof, to perform a task or set of tasks. "Software"includes only those copies of information, programs, or routinesintended for use by an end user and specifically excludes retainedrights in software and master copies of software. "Software" includesthe associated documentation that describes the code and its use,operation, and maintenance and typically is delivered with the code tothe consumer. All software is classified as either canned or custom. (3) The sale of canned software, other than a sale to a person whopresents a resale certificate under RCW 82.04.470, regardless of themethod of delivery to the end user, shall be taxed as a retail sale.Any sale of canned software which is not a sale at retail shall betaxed as a wholesale sale. The licensing of canned software to an enduser shall be taxed as a sale, not as a royalty or otherwise ascompensation for the use of intangible property. The sale of customsoftware, or the customization of canned software, shall be taxed as aservice, not a sale. (4) The production of canned software in a city shall be taxed asmanufacturing. HB 1747 p. 2 (5) The creation and distribution of custom software is taxable asa service activity. Duplication of the software for the same person,or by the same person for its own use, does not change the character ofthe software. The customization of canned software is taxable as aservice activity.
